analysis: The candidate succeeded: reported validation HR@10 increased from 0.645 to 0.665, an absolute gain of 0.020, equivalent to four additional hits among 200 validation users. This exceeded the proposed 0.655 target. The selected checkpoint was at epoch 15. WEIGHT_DECAY=0.00001 was the only intended change, making modest Adam L2 regularization promising for this architecture. The result is consistent with improved generalization but does not establish the mechanism or robustness across seeds. The host reports 35 completed epochs versus the planned 30, so exact protocol equivalence should not be assumed. No test metric was reported.
code_summary: Position-free causal NextItNet with tied 64-dimensional item embeddings and eight independent residual blocks using dilations [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8]. Each block mixes local and dilated width-3 convolutions using a sigmoid gate, then applies a second dilated convolution, with LayerNorm, GELU, dropout, and learned per-channel residual scales initialized to 0.1. Left padding preserves causality; padding positions are masked after each block. Final normalized states score items by embedding dot products; candidate scoring uses the last nonpadding state. Configuration: MAXLEN=128, HIDDEN_UNITS=64, NUM_BLOCKS=8, KERNEL_SIZE=3, DROPOUT_RATE=0.2, LR=0.001, WEIGHT_DECAY=0.00001, BATCH_SIZE=128. Preserve this architecture and retain modest weight decay as a promising setting for subsequent comparisons.
